e: AWS Shield Advanced protects the ALB against DDoS attacks with little configuration, gives access to the DDoS Response Team (DRT), and provides attack diagnostics and visibility for auditing sources. WAF rules for unknown IPs can't handle random-source DDoS, and Inspector isn't a DDoS service.

Import the Snowball data into S3, then use an FSx for Lustre file system linked to the bucket, which gives the HPC cluster consistent sub-millisecond latency and high throughput on the data. File gateway and EFS have higher latency, and data can't be imported directly into FSx from a Snowball Edge device.

A DataSync agent can periodically copy NFS data to S3 with little setup and you pay per GB transferred, which suits small periodic backups cost-effectively. Glue isn't an on-premises copy tool, and Transfer for SFTP or Direct Connect add recurring costs.

A Network Load Balancer handles UDP traffic with ultra-low latency and millions of requests per second at a lower cost. ALBs don't support UDP, Gateway Load Balancers are for virtual appliances, and duplicating servers in other Regions adds cost.

Migrating MySQL to Aurora PostgreSQL is a heterogeneous migration: AWS DMS Schema Conversion transforms the schema and database objects, and a DMS task with change data capture (CDC) migrates the data and replicates ongoing changes during the migration. Aurora PostgreSQL read replicas of a MySQL instance are impossible.

A read replica takes the reporting script's load off the primary database (the Multi-AZ standby can't serve reads), is simple to set up, and doesn't need code changes beyond the endpoint. Manual exports or caches add work or don't reduce load.

ALB access logs stored in S3 can be queried with Athena using SQL to analyze client IPs, request patterns, and errors with little setup. CloudTrail doesn't log ALB requests, and manual file review or EMR is inefficient.

A public NAT gateway must be placed in a public subnet (with a route to the internet gateway), and the private subnets' route tables point their default route to it so instances can reach the internet. Private NAT gateways don't provide internet access, and a NAT in a private subnet has no internet path.

The SCP must apply only to the nonproduction accounts: attach it directly to those three member accounts, or place them in a new OU and attach the SCP to that OU. Attaching it to the root OU or management account would affect production too.

A VPC endpoint (gateway endpoint) for S3 gives a private connection from the EC2 instances to S3 that doesn't use the internet, and the bucket policy can restrict access to that endpoint. IAM policies, NAT gateways, and access keys don't make the connection private.

Adding Aurora reader instances scales read capacity and provides failover targets, and RDS Proxy pools connections and speeds up failover, reducing timeouts and downtime. Logging via Lambda, ZDR with activity streams, or a Redis write-around cache don't scale reads and writes with little downtime.

A Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint with a forwarding rule associated with the VPC lets resources in the VPC resolve private DNS names hosted on premises over the VPN, securely. Inbound endpoints are for on-premises to AWS resolution, and hosted zones don't resolve on-premises records.

S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves photos between tiers as their access changes (some viewed for months, others for less than a week), which is cost-effective, and DynamoDB holds metadata and S3 locations for fast lookups. DynamoDB isn't suited to 20 MB photos (400 KB item limit), and Glacier classes aren't for viewable photos.

The ALB's least outstanding requests routing algorithm sends new requests to the targets with the fewest in-flight requests, so overloaded instances don't receive more. The scenario's indicators are the RequestCount and TargetResponseTime metrics, while round robin keeps sending requests regardless of load.

A Savings Plans alert subscription (in the Savings Plans console) notifies by email when utilization or coverage drops below the threshold, which is the simplest, most efficient way to be notified. Custom Lambda reports or budget reports need more setup.

To make MSK publicly reachable, place the cluster in public subnets of the existing VPC and secure it with TLS and mutual TLS authentication so data in transit is encrypted, with no need to build a new VPC. ALB or NLB in private subnets don't expose Kafka to the internet.

An internal Transfer Family SFTP server across two AZs (reachable from the on-premises ERP over the existing connectivity) stores files in S3, and a Transfer Family managed workflow invokes Lambda right when a file arrives, so orders are processed immediately in a secure, resilient design. Hourly polling and single-AZ servers don't meet the requirements.

Amazon EMR on AWS Outposts runs managed Hadoop and Spark on premises with scalable, managed infrastructure, which reduces complexity while keeping data processing on premises. The other options move processing or data to AWS.

FSx for NetApp ONTAP supports both SMB and NFS for Windows, Mac, and Linux clients, and its auto tiering policy moves infrequently accessed data to a cheaper tier automatically, with low overhead. EFS doesn't support SMB, S3 File Gateway runs on premises, and FSx for OpenZFS lacks SMB.

Breaking the monolith into microservices on Amazon ECS with service auto scaling makes it flexible, scalable, and gradually improvable, and rolling updates to individual services avoid downtime. A single Lambda function can't run a long monolith well, Spot Instances can interrupt reports, and all-at-once Beanstalk deployments cause downtime.

AWS Lambda supports Python, scales automatically to hundreds of requests per second, and needs no servers or operations, which is ideal for a serverless microservice. EC2 fleets, Elastic Beanstalk, and EKS need more infrastructure management.

A transit gateway with the Direct Connect connection attached through a transit VIF (Direct Connect gateway association) and route propagation connects all 30 VPCs and on-premises networks centrally with the least overhead. Peering meshes, per-VPC VPNs, or virtual private gateways don't scale as simply.

Enabling Default Host Management Configuration in Systems Manager grants managed access to the instances automatically without changing the instances' existing IAM roles, so patching doesn't disrupt the running applications. Replacing role policies would break database access, and IAM users aren't used for instance management.

The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler scales pods but not nodes, so the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler is needed to add nodes when pods can't be scheduled, with little administrative effort. Lambda scripts or a plain Auto Scaling group don't react to pod scheduling.

Frequent multipart uploads of 50 GB objects leave incomplete parts behind that are stored and billed, so costs grow while the visible objects stay constant. A lifecycle rule that deletes incomplete multipart uploads removes the hidden storage. Transfer Acceleration, inventory, and CloudFront don't remove these parts.
